records.name: South Philadelphia Shtiebel
records.summary: A Jewish community in South Philadelphia for prayer, learning and friendship. The site lists a Zoom room for prayer and study, a Slack group for members, and a kiddush sponsorship for family milestones.
records.what_you_do: Join prayer and learning on the Zoom room, take part in the Slack community, or sponsor a kiddush after a life milestone.

first_step.how: Use the Zoom room link on the site, or email the group for a Slack invitation
first_step.basis: Prayer and learning are open online with a clear way to join, but the site does not describe an in-person visit.

records.notes: No worship days or times are published, so no schedule is recorded. The site has no dated events or news; its only year is a footer copyright, which is not evidence. A separate Slack request address is published and not recorded.

records.name: Mekom Torah
records.summary: An online study group for Jewish adults. It offers Hebrew courses, reading groups and a discussion group called Exploring Judaism, which needs no Hebrew to join.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a Hebrew course, join a reading group, or take part in the Exploring Judaism discussions on Zoom when they are running.

schedule.text: Exploring Judaism meets on Zoom two Thursdays a month at 2 pm Eastern, October to May. The site says the group is on sabbatical right now. Reading the Tradition in Hebrew meets every other Sunday, with no time listed.

first_step.how: Use the sign up link on the How to Read Hebrew page, or contact the group by phone or its contact page
first_step.basis: The site says Exploring Judaism needs no Hebrew and is open to everyone, and it links a sign up page for each course.

records.notes: Mailing address is in West Townshend, Vermont, and no Philadelphia address is listed. Recorded because the courses are online and open to anyone, including Philadelphia residents. The Exploring Judaism group is paused for a sabbatical, so check before promoting it. The email address on the contact page is obscured and not recorded. How to Read Hebrew was listed to begin September 28, 2026.

records.name: Jewish Children's Folkshul
records.summary: A secular Jewish community in Northwest Philadelphia for families and adults. Its Sunday school teaches Jewish history, holidays and values to children from kindergarten through high school, and adults can join study groups, outings and social clubs.
records.what_you_do: Enroll children in Sunday school, come to holiday celebrations and life-cycle events as a family, or join adult study groups, outings and social activities.

schedule.text: Sunday school meets on Sundays from 10 am to 12:30 pm.

locations.label: Northwest Philadelphia (street address shared by email)

cost.text: Tuition and dues not stated; donations are invited for the High Holidays

first_step.how: Register for Sunday school through the site, or email the group for location and visit details
first_step.basis: Families and adults can register or email for a visit, but the page does not say newcomers are welcomed by name.

records.notes: The calendar lists Oct 11 and Oct 18 sessions with no year written, so no sign of life date is recorded. The only year on the page is the copyright line. The mailing address is a PO Box in Lafayette Hill, while the site says it meets in Northwest Philadelphia. Kind set to congregation because it holds lifecycle ceremonies.

records.name: Spruce Street Minyan
records.summary: An egalitarian prayer group for Jewish people in their 20s and 30s who live in Philadelphia. It holds a monthly Friday night service followed by a shared Shabbat meal.
records.what_you_do: Come to the monthly Friday night service and stay for the Shabbat meal, sign up to volunteer, or email the group to introduce yourself.

schedule.text: A Friday evening service once a month, followed by a Shabbat meal. Upcoming services are listed for Oct 16, 2026 and Nov 13, 2026. RSVP is required.

first_step.how: RSVP on OneTable for a service, or email the group to introduce yourself
first_step.basis: Services are public and listed with a clear RSVP route and an email, but the page does not say newcomers are welcomed by name.

records.notes: No street address is published. The Sunday niggun circle on Oct 18 has no year written, so it is not used for dating. The footer year is a copyright line and is not evidence. Facebook and Instagram links exist on the site and were not read.

records.name: Moishe House Philadelphia
records.summary: A Jewish young adult house in Philadelphia that hosts gatherings for people in their 20s and their friends. Recent listings include a talk, a nigun circle and a wine tasting.
records.what_you_do: Come to an open house event such as a talk, a nigun circle or a tasting after contacting the house. The site also links to a resident program.

schedule.text: Events are listed with evening times, roughly 6 to 9 pm. Listings on the page are Oct 8, Oct 18 and Oct 22, with no year written. There is no fixed weekly schedule.

first_step.how: Email the house or use the contact form on the page to ask about an event
first_step.basis: The page calls the house welcoming and inclusive and gives a clear contact route, but it does not describe a newcomer program.

records.notes: The house was listed at moishehouse.org and now redirects to memglobal.org; the redirect was followed. Event dates have no year written, so no sign of life date is recorded. The only dated item with a year is a December 2026 camp promotion, which is not a house event. The community manager's staff address was seen and left out.

records.name: Female Hebrew Benevolent Society of Philadelphia
records.summary: A Philadelphia charity, founded in 1819, that helps local Jewish women in financial need. It gives emergency grants and monthly stipends, funds medical alert systems for frail older women, and pays for camp scholarships.
records.what_you_do: Women in financial need can email the charity to ask about help. Others can donate online or write to the office with questions.

cost.text: The site does not state fees; aid is for eligible women

first_step.how: Email info@fhbs.org to ask about help or how to get involved; the site does not describe an application
first_step.basis: Help is for local Jewish women in financial crisis, but the page does not say how to apply or where to start.

records.notes: The site reports activity for the fiscal year ended April 30, 2025, which is the newest dated evidence used. Its newest dated news item is from October 10, 2023. Eligibility rules and an application process are not published. Board members are not recorded.

records.name: Hadassah Greater Philadelphia Region
records.summary: The Greater Philadelphia region of Hadassah, the Women's Zionist Organization of America. Its chapters cover most of Pennsylvania and Wilmington, Delaware, and focus on health, social action and community events.
records.what_you_do: Join a local chapter for programs and social events, sign up for the Greater Philadelphia email list, or come to the High Tea hosted by the Shalom Tamid chapter on Oct 29, 2026.

cost.text: Dues and event fees not stated

first_step.how: Use the Connect Locally page to find a chapter, or join the Greater Philadelphia email list
first_step.basis: Joining means membership with dues, and the page does not say whether guests can attend events before joining.

records.notes: Regional page only; chapter pages were not read. The text read did not state a religious identity, so faith is left blank. The High Tea time is not listed, and it has an online option. Kind set to club because membership and chapters are the way in.

records.name: TacklingTorah
records.summary: A rabbi-led service for Jewish life-cycle moments, plus a blog about Jewish ritual at home.
records.notes: Not recorded as a group: it is a ritual and life-cycle service with no classes, meetings or events listed. Pricing is not stated. The newest dated item is a 2019 blog post. The page gives no street address or city, so a Philadelphia location is not confirmed.

leads_only.name: B'nai Abraham Chabad
leads_only.note: Congregation at 527 Lombard St, seen in a search result about Chabad Young Philly. Not fetched because the search budget was used up.

blocked.note: 403 recorded by the earlier agent (r-jewish-congregations). Not retried, so no record.

notes: Input had 15 leads, all Jewish. Result: 7 publish, 1 not_a_group, 7 not recorded. Not recorded: (1) Chabad Young Philly, now Mamash! Chabad at 1601 and 1603 Lombard St. One search found only a July 2021 Jewish Exponent article and a 2019 Inquirer piece, with no current website, contact or dated listing, so it was skipped rather than written as dormant. (2) jkidphilly, Jewish Learning Venture, Philadelphia Jewish Film and Media and One Table each returned only the page title with a truncation notice on two or more fetches. Worth a later retry. (3) Moishe House RSJ: the redirected memglobal.org page returned 404, so its status is unknown. (4) Makom Community: 403 from the earlier agent, not retried. Moishe House sites moved to memglobal.org and the server redirect was followed. Dates written without a year (Folkshul Oct 11 and 18, Moishe House Oct 8, 18 and 22, Spruce niggun circle Oct 18) were not turned into 2026 dates. Copyright footers were not used as evidence. Search budget: 1 of 1 used. Fetches: about 19, including redirects. No rate limiting was seen.
